patches.instructions: Register wgsl/q4_gemv_smallm_v2.wgsl and wgsl/q4_gate_up_swiglu_smallm_v2.wgsl as new shader ids. Route scalar decode (M=1), chain verify, tree verify and rejection replay through the SAME V2 family per precision tier. Dispatch (ceil(rows/64),1,1) for every M in 1..16; bindings 0 uniform (8 words: rows, cols, weight offset u32, input offset f32, output offset f32, residual flag, M, kernel arg), 1 weights, 2 activations, 3 output. Plain: arg = output stride (0 = rows). Fused: arg = up-weight offset (u32), dense output. Use a dedicated fused descriptor (do not reuse the last uniform word trick of the old path). Remove the second weight traversal for M > 8.
patches.rationale: Scalar and batched Q4 used different block grouping and reduction order, so equal rows could round differently (one-block witness in the Cycle 15 audit).
patches.verify: Every row bit-identical at M=1..16 including LM-head shards (stride = vocab, odd row counts, non-zero offsets); the repo test tests/q4SmallMV2.test.ts encodes the same cases.

patches.appliedWhen: this\.rollback\.defer\(rbEnc\.finish\(\)\)|P9a: queue order already makes every later submit see the restored state
patches.rationale: The reject branch waited for the rollback (second submit + onSubmittedWorkDone) before returning, which is the fence round trip inside the measured 3.67 ms M=5 reject surcharge. Every later GPU operation is queued behind the rollback, and every later readback (mapAsync) resolves after it, so the wait adds latency without adding ordering. Device loss surfaces at the next mapAsync, as for any step.
patches.verify: Forced-rejection replay (P1b verify) still equals serial decode; rc1-speculative microbench t5RejectMs - t5Ms drops; abort mid-turn and device-loss paths unchanged.

patches.replace: this.rollback.defer(rbEnc.finish()); // P9b: runs at the head of the next submission
patches.rationale: Encode the rollback at reject time but submit it with the next verify step (one queue.submit with two command buffers) or at the next flush point. Requires P9b-rollback-flush-guards.
patches.verify: tests/rollbackP9.test.ts simulator semantics; live: 45-pair greedy parity and the forced-rejection replay test.

patches.rationale: The chain-verify hot path writes only tokenIdsBuf and its per-plan uniform buffer before submitting, neither of which the rollback reads, so prepending the pending rollback preserves queue order and saves the extra submit.
patches.verify: As P9b-rollback-defer-reject.

patches.instructions: Copy ts/rc1/rollbackScheduler.ts into src/offscreen. Add the field `private rollback = new DeferredRollback<GPUCommandBuffer>((cbs) => this.device!.queue.submit(cbs));`. Call `this.rollback.flush(point)` as the FIRST statement (before any writeBuffer, buffer creation or readback) of: decodeStep (decode-step), prefill and prefillChunk (prefill), the background/context prefill entry (prefill-background), saveGpuPrefixSlot (slot-save), restoreGpuPrefixSlot (slot-restore), resetState (reset), snapshotState (snapshot), restoreState (restore-snapshot), decodeSpeculativeTreeStep (tree-step), and the growth branch of ensureKvCapacity before any allocation or copy (kv-grow). Call flush('end-of-turn') when a generate run completes or aborts, and `this.rollback.discard()` in dispose and on device loss. Keep the rollback's writeBuffer into prefillUniformBuf at reject time: every entry point that writes prefillUniformBuf flushes first, so that write stays ahead of the next one in queue order.
patches.rationale: Deferral is safe only if no GPU work or writeBuffer that touches what the rollback reads (DeltaNet state, backups, saved norm rows or stashed projections, prefillUniformBuf, workBuf) lands between the reject and the rollback, and no buffer it references is reallocated first.
patches.verify: tests/rollbackP9.test.ts: 400 random transition sequences through every flush point equal the blocking rollback bit-for-bit; removing a flush (prefill, reset) or merging after the next snapshot is detected.
